statement:
For all natural \(n\), an \(n\)-staircase is a figure consisting of unit squares with one square in the first row, two in the second, and so on up to \(n\) in the \(n\)-th row, with all leftmost squares aligned vertically. Let \(f(n)\) denote the minimum number of square tiles (of any natural-number side length) needed to tile the \(n\)-staircase.

(a) Find all \(n\) such that \(f(n) = n\).

(b) Find all \(n\) such that \(f(n) = n + 1\).

Let \(A\), \(B\), \(P\) be three points on a circle. Prove that if \(a\) and \(b\) are the distances from \(P\) to the tangents to the circle at \(A\) and \(B\) respectively, and \(c\) is the distance from \(P\) to the chord \(AB\), then \(c^2 = ab\).

Three speed skaters start from the same point on an oval and skate in the same direction with constant speeds: the slowest does \(1\) lap per minute, the fastest does \(3.14\) laps per minute, and the middle one does \(L\) laps per minute for some \(1 < L < 3.14\). The race ends when all three skaters are again at the same point on the oval. Determine the number of different choices for \(L\) such that exactly \(117\) passings occur before the end of the race. (A passing occurs when one skater passes another; the start and end moments are not counted.)

Each vertex of a finite graph can be coloured either black or white. Initially all vertices are black. We may pick any vertex \(P\) and toggle the colour of \(P\) and all its neighbours. Is it possible, by a sequence of such operations, to change every vertex from black to white?

Let \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) be polynomials with integer coefficients. Let \(a_n = n! + n\). Show that if \(\dfrac{P(a_n)}{Q(a_n)}\) is an integer for every \(n\), then \(\dfrac{P(n)}{Q(n)}\) is an integer for every integer \(n\) with \(Q(n) \neq 0\).
